comments.value:
I'm really sorry that happened to you, that's disturbing. >.< That's definitely someone that needs to be reported.

Unfortunately, I really don't know how well people would take this feature. It is possible to do, as I've seen it done in Second Life, but people will also be against it for privacy concerns or even worried about false reports.

I can think of a way to integrate this, though, like having an option to see 3rd person cameras when you have your menu or quick menu open, like how we already do with the in-game film camera, including the direction they're facing.

In Second Life, there is a feature to view where peoples' cameras are, hidden in a debug menu, but I did see first hand how this feature was used to harass people. There were sometimes people who would start harassing you if they saw you were even so much as looking at them or if they *thought* you were looking at them. I'm sure some people have gone out of their way to get their friends together to all stare at a single person that was like that, only making things worse. A very real response to this I have seen was people putting weird meshes on their avatars that make it impossible for someone to look directly at them, which would often end up being intrusive for everyone else. (Some people made these objects massive.) Second Life also ended up implementing a debug option to disable sending the camera information, which pretty much put everything back at square one. Still to this day there's a lot of people in Second Life who will pick a fight with you just because you moved your camera close to them and it's not fun when that happens. In my experience, all this did in Second Life was reinforce my eye-contact issues because I felt like I wasn't allowed to look at anybody or anything because apparently being perceived in of itself was rude to some people.

The main difference between VRChat and Second Life, though, is that Second Life allowed you to just free your camera at will and move it around wherever you pleased. VRChat only does that with the camera and drone systems, not 3rd person view, so I don't know how different things would be.

I personally am willing to give this feature a shot in a VR environment. I don't want people being harassed, but I also don't want to see people getting absolutely paranoid over where people are looking 24/7 like on Second Life. It's unfortunately a "pick your poison" ordeal.

details: When using third-person view, please make it clear where your viewpoint is. You might not mind if you're dealing with an NPC, but it's not something you should do when dealing with a real human avatar. Someone is staring at my crotch from behind a building today, wetting their underwear. Well, if that's the purpose of VRChat, I don't care.
title: When using third-person view, make sure it's clear where the viewpoint is.
